questions.q: Define situational irony and give one example from "नसोलसुक का छंद" where the character's expectation contradicts the actual outcome.
questions.a: Situational irony occurs when the outcome of a situation is sharply contrary to what was expected or intended. In "नसोलसुक का छंद," Nasolsuk's husband joins the freedom struggle expecting to secure a better future for his family, but his absence leaves her destitute and vulnerable — the very freedom he fights for bypasses his own home. A wrong answer (e.g., "irony is when someone lies") reveals confusion between verbal irony (saying the opposite) and situational irony (outcome vs expectation), and inability to locate the device in the specific textual context.

questions.q: In "डाकुसफ्याक का छंद," the line "वृक्ष की जड़ें गहरी हैं, शाखाएँ फैली हैं" uses the tree as a symbol. Explain in your own words what abstract idea this symbol represents and why the poet chooses a tree rather than a building or a river.
questions.a: The tree symbolizes Indian civilization/composite culture: deep roots = ancient heritage and shared history; spreading branches = diverse communities, languages, religions growing from the same trunk. A tree is chosen because it is organic, living, interdependent (roots feed branches, leaves feed roots), and resilient — unlike a building (static, man-made, collapses) or a river (flows away, no visible unity). A wrong answer listing only "unity" or "strength" without the root/branch mapping shows superficial symbol-decoding; missing the organic metaphor reveals failure to analyze why this specific vehicle (tree) carries the tenor (nation).

questions.q: Apply the concept of dramatic irony to the moment in "नसोलसुक का छंद" where Nasolsuk addresses her absent husband: "तुम्हारे लिए मैंने सब सहा." Who knows more than the speaker at this moment, and how does that knowledge gap create irony?
questions.a: Dramatic irony arises when the audience/reader knows something a character does not. Here, the reader knows (from the poem's context) that the husband's "freedom" has not brought relief to Nasolsuk; the system exploits both. She believes her suffering serves a noble cause; we see it serves a patriarchal-colonial structure that ignores women. The knowledge gap: Nasolsuk thinks sacrifice = redemption; reader sees sacrifice = erasure. A wrong answer confusing this with situational irony ("she expected X, got Y") misses the structural reader-character knowledge asymmetry that defines dramatic irony.

questions.q: Compare the function of "नक़ली फूल" (artificial flowers) in "नसोलसुक का छंद" with "पक्षी" (birds) in "डाकुसफ्याक का छंद." Both are symbols — but one signifies falseness, the other freedom. Analyze how each symbol's meaning is derived from its physical properties in the poem.
questions.a: "नक़ली फूल" — made of paper/cloth, never wilt, no fragrance, mass-produced — symbolize hollow rituals, performative patriotism, and the fake honors bestowed on women's suffering. Their physical lifelessness maps to emotional/spiritual emptiness. "पक्षी" — fly freely across branches, nest in the tree, sing diverse songs — symbolize citizens/communities finding shelter and expression in the composite nation. Their mobility and song map to liberty and cultural pluralism. A wrong answer that merely labels them "symbols of bad/good" without linking physical trait → abstract meaning shows inability to do semiotic analysis (signifier → signified).

questions.q: Evaluate this claim: "The irony in 'नसोलसुक का छंद' weakens the poem's feminist critique because it makes the woman appear passive." Defend or refute using textual evidence.
questions.a: Refute. The irony *is* the critique: it exposes how patriarchal nationalism conscripts women's labor ("मैंने हक़ीक़त का बोझ उठाया") while denying them agency. Nasolsuk's final lines — "दुनिया! तुम इसे न छीन पाओगी / इससे प्यार की गंध आती है" — reclaim voice. The irony highlights systemic betrayal, not female passivity. A wrong answer agreeing with the claim misses that irony here targets the *structure*, not the victim; it also ignores the poem's closing resistance, revealing a reading that stops at victimhood without tracing the arc to assertion.

questions.q: Create a four-line stanza using *both* irony and symbolism to depict a modern Indian student who studies "Digital India" by candlelight during a power cut. Use a concrete object as symbol and an outcome-expectation gap as irony.
questions.a:
Example stanza:
"डिजिटल इंडिया का पाठ पढ़ता हूँ दीये की रोशनी में,
लैपटॉप बंद, बैटरी मरी — भविष्य अंधेरे में चमकता है।
किताब का पन्ना (प्रतीक: ज्ञान जो बिजली नहीं माँगता)
हवा के झोंके से फड़फड़ाता है — असली नेटवर्क यही है।"
Symbol: किताब का पन्ना = resilient, non-digital knowledge. Irony: studying a digital future in analog darkness. A poor answer uses only metaphor ("candle = hope") without irony, or only irony ("power cut during Digital India class") without a developed symbol, showing inability to integrate both devices organically.
